name: Redis bundled jemalloc: an address-hinted extent mapping must land exactly on the hint or be discarded
required_postconditions: when addr != NULL, mmap must return exactly addr; anything else is unmapped again and treated as failure
MAP_FIXED must NOT be used, because it would replace an existing mapping instead of failing - jemalloc says so in the code
the resulting extent abuts the caller's existing extent, which is what makes coalescing in the extent map legal

failure_sink.description: on a relocated result os_pages_map calls os_pages_unmap(ret, size) at pages.c:160 and returns NULL. The caller (pages_map -> pages_map_slow) then retries once with the over-allocate-and-trim strategy, which does not require identity. A relocation costs one wasted syscall pair, never correctness.

source_locations.symbol: comment: 'We don't use MAP_FIXED here, because it can cause the *replacement* of existing mappings, and we only want to create new mappings.'
ret = mmap(addr, size, prot, mmap_flags, PAGES_FD_TAG, 0);
} else if (addr != NULL && ret != addr) { - the identity check
assert(ret == NULL || (addr == NULL && ret != addr) || (addr != NULL && ret == addr));

extraction_limitations: `addr` here is a runtime value computed by the extent allocator from an existing extent's end; there is no compile-time constant to put in request.address, so the field is left absent. This is the ordinary case for an allocator and it is exactly the case rule_hinted_relocation cannot see, because that rule begins with `if (!req_.request.address) return;`
2MiB is a representative extent size, not a constant in the source

permitted_fallbacks is documented as 'what the program is willing to accept instead of the exact request', which is a program-level question, so 'relocate' is recorded: jemalloc as a whole does accept a relocated mapping, via pages_map_slow. But the identity postcondition belongs to the os_pages_map CALL, which accepts nothing. The schema attaches one fallback list to one MappingRequest and so cannot separate 'this call must be exact' from 'the enclosing algorithm has a relaxed second attempt'. This try-exact-then-relax shape is the normal way allocators are written

x_campaign.rationale: permitted_fallbacks contains relocate while guest_host_identity_required is true, so rule_internal_fallback_contradiction (RS-VM-0014) should fire Proven/Unsupported and suppress everything else. I expect that to be wrong: jemalloc's try-exact-then-relax structure is not a contradiction, it is two attempts with different contracts, and the schema has only one fallback list per request to describe both.
